A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GROOD. Their complete main text, equations, tables, figures, algorithms, and appendices are readable and matchable. v3 adds Appendix A.7 to the material retained from v2.

before.justification: v2 reports original GROOD detection experiments, oracle experiments, ablations, checkpoint analyses, and inference timings.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds an experiment on a manifold-mixup-trained backbone in Appendix A.7.

M1.justification: Prototype generation, gradient computation, and nearest-neighbor scoring are unchanged. The mean-prototype variant used in the new backbone experiment already appears in v2 Appendix A.2 and Table 6; it is not a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same four core ID datasets, near/far-OOD datasets, and auxiliary or corrupted validation data. Appendix A.7 retains CIFAR-100 detection and changes the backbone training condition, not dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds fdbd (Liu and Qin, 2023) and NCI (Liu and Qin, 2025). All previous table comparators remain, although several rows are reordered.

E3.justification: Appendix A.7 adds evaluation of a manifold-mixup-trained ResNet-18 on CIFAR-100 using the mean-prototype variant. This introduces a new backbone training condition. Newly supplied training budgets for the main experiments do not establish that those experiments were changed or rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix A.7 and Table 7 add a robustness case examining prototype use with a mixup-trained backbone, comparing GROOD with ASH, KNN, and GradNorm. Existing component ablations, prototype comparisons, checkpoint analyses, density plots, and neighbor-count sensitivity results are retained.

E5.justification: The three-seed evaluations, single-seed ImageNet-1k reporting, five auxiliary-data selections, and checkpoint standard-deviation analysis are unchanged. Table 7 introduces no new uncertainty estimation or reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Shared table values are unchanged. v3 adds fdbd/NCI scores, Table 7 results (GROOD: 81.05% near-OOD, 80.26% far-OOD), and a CombOOD comparison with unspecified matching conditions. Section 6 corrects GROOD's ImageNet-1k far-OOD prose from 94.57% to 94.8%, but incorrectly calls VIM's CIFAR-100 far-OOD score of 81.70% a near-OOD result; Table 2 gives 74.98% near-OOD.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9 and the closed-form derivation in Appendix A.6 are unchanged. The expanded Euclidean-distance discussion motivates the existing gradient norm and direction properties without adding a formal result or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and four contribution statements retain their scientific claims. The revised introduction emphasizes near-OOD detection, architectural generalization, and checkpoint stability already claimed and discussed in v2.

C2.justification: v3 adds a specific caveat about synthetic mixup samples' limited diversity and recommends adapting prototype choice to mixup-trained backbones. It also expands the neural-collapse and distance-metric rationale and reframes the results around near/far-OOD trade-offs. Existing clustering, noise, and storage limitations remain.

D1.justification: Section 6 newly documents the 100-epoch SGD schedule, optimizer parameters, learning-rate decay, batch sizes, and 30-epoch fine-tuning settings. It replaces the anonymous code link with a named GitHub repository link. These are documentation and access-information changes; repository availability was not externally checked.

R1.justification: v3 adds references and comparisons involving fdbd, NCI, and CombOOD, and removes Shu et al.'s P-ODN citation and reference. The results discussion additionally emphasizes training-free deployment relative to other approaches; the related-work survey is otherwise substantially retained.

P1.justification: Selected introduction, methodology, results-discussion, and conclusion paragraphs are rewritten or condensed. Affiliations are updated, acknowledgments are added, and Appendix A.7 is appended. The main section order and much of the prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 2 is expanded and reordered, Table 7 is added, and Figure 2's caption is shortened. Figures, tables, and algorithms shift with text reflow. All five existing figures retain identical graphics.

improvement.justification: Explicit training details, an identified repository link, updated baseline comparisons, and the focused backbone experiment modestly improve documentation and empirical assessment. These gains are limited by the new VIM near/far-OOD misreading and by Appendix A.7's missing direct comparison between synthetic and mean prototypes on the mixup-trained backbone, leaving its preference claim insufficiently supported.
